_note: Hand-written scene for each card, true to the myth, keyed by card id. build_manifest.py uses it in place of the automatic subject line. Edit a line, re-run build_manifest.py, then regenerate that card with --ids <id> --force.

ody.spear: A seasoned Ithacan spearman, a grown soldier in a simple bronze helmet and linen cuirass, braced behind a round bronze shield, spear levelled, on the rocky shore of Ithaca with a dark sea behind him at dusk.
ody.sailor: A sailor of Odysseus's fleet straining at the oar of a black-hulled Greek ship with painted eyes on its prow, spray flying, the wine-dark sea at dusk.
ody.spearc: A bronze-tipped spear hurled across the plain of Troy in a duel before the city walls, caught mid-flight, dust and a blood-red setting sun behind it.
ody.aegis: Athena's aegis, the goatskin cloak fringed with golden serpents and bearing the Gorgon's head, spread in divine light over a kneeling Greek warrior.
ody.camp: A ragged camp follower in the Greek camp on the beach at Troy, carrying a basket and a water jar between the beached black ships and smoking cook-fires.
ody.sent: An Argive sentinel on night watch on the earthen wall the Greeks built to guard their ships at Troy, a tall shield planted beside him, watch-fires behind.
ody.hopl: An Argive warrior behind a towering Mycenaean figure-of-eight body shield, wearing a boar's-tusk helmet as Homer describes, braced and immovable on the plain of Troy.
ody.gate: A guard standing before the Lion Gate of Mycenae, two carved lionesses above the massive stone lintel, his spear barring the way, torchlight on the stone.
ody.ajax: Ajax the Great, giant of the Greeks, standing guard before the beached Greek ships behind his huge tower shield of seven ox-hides faced with bronze, calm and immovable, watch-fires glowing in the night behind him.
ody.rampart: The towering walls of Troy, which the myths say Poseidon and Apollo built, seen from below at dusk, torches burning along the battlements.
ody.doct: A disciplined phalanx seen head-on: rows of round bronze shields locked rim to rim, spears held upright, crested helmets, dust rising around them.
ody.hearth: The great hearth of Odysseus's hall on Ithaca, the fire burning low; in the shadows Penelope's loom holds the burial shroud she weaves by day and unravels by night.
ody.drill: Greek soldiers drilling in formation on a dusty training ground beneath a mountain, a scarred old instructor shouting the time.
ody.wall: A wall of round aspis shields painted with bold emblems (a scorpion, a Gorgon's face, a charging bull), locked together, seen close up.
ody.testudo: Warriors crouched under a locked roof of shields as a rain of arrows and stones falls on them from a city wall.
ody.shield: The Shield of Achilles that the smith god Hephaestus forged, its bronze face worked in rings showing earth, sea, sky, cities at peace and at war, glowing on the anvil of his forge.
ody.thess: A Thessalian horseman galloping across the plains of Thessaly, cloak streaming, javelin raised, a storm sky over the mountains behind.
ody.zerk: A frenzied warrior possessed by Ares, eyes wild, mouth open in a war cry, charging, while the war god's red shadow looms behind him in the smoke.
ody.agam: Agamemnon, king of Mycenae and leader of the Greek host at Troy, in gold-trimmed armour, raising his ancestral sceptre to rally the army before the ships.
ody.achil: Achilles in the divine armour Hephaestus made him, leaping forward with his great ash spear, the plain and walls of Troy behind him, his one vulnerable heel just visible.
ody.fury: Ares, god of war, in a crested helmet and wreathed in red fire, gripping a mortal warrior's arm and filling him with sudden battle-rage.
ody.rally: A herald on a hilltop blowing a war horn as the scattered Greek warriors below rise and turn back toward the fight.
ody.spoils: A heap of plunder on a beach beside a black ship: bronze tripods, golden cups, captured armour and shields, glinting in torchlight.
ody.banner: A war standard on a tall pole, a crimson banner snapping in the wind over the Greek camp at Troy, the beached black ships behind.
ody.ares: The great bronze spear of Ares, god of war, standing upright in scorched earth, smoke and embers swirling around it on a ruined battlefield.
ody.ox: A white ox with gilded horns and a garland of flowers being led to the altar for sacrifice, as in the Homeric rites, smoke and a priest waiting.
ody.argus: Argus, Odysseus's old hound, lying worn and neglected by the palace gate on Ithaca, lifting his head and wagging his tail as he recognises his master, returned after twenty years disguised as a beggar.
ody.pythia: The Pythia, the oracle of Delphi, seated on a bronze tripod in the dark inner temple, entranced, holding a laurel sprig as vapours rise around her.
ody.telem: Telemachus, the grown son of Odysseus, standing at the prow of a ship leaving Ithaca to seek news of his father, the goddess Athena beside him disguised as old Mentor.
ody.cass: Cassandra, the cursed prophetess of Troy, wild-haired and crying out her warning that no one believes, as the great wooden horse is dragged through the gates behind her.
ody.hecat: A hecatomb, the great sacrifice of a hundred oxen: altar fires burning in a row along the seashore, thick smoke rising to the gods.
ody.altar: A stone altar heaped with votive offerings, small clay figurines, garlands and burning fat, glowing in a dark sanctuary.
ody.zeus: A white marble altar of Zeus on a mountain-top at night, offering smoke rising from it, a crackling bolt of lightning striking down onto the altar from a storm-black sky.
ody.pyre: A towering funeral pyre burning on the beach at Troy at night, like the pyre of Patroclus, sparks spiralling up to the stars.
ody.ossuary: The inside of a beehive tomb like the Treasury of Atreus at Mycenae: bones, bronze helmets and grave gifts laid in the dark, a single shaft of light from the doorway.
ody.requiem: Mourners lamenting over a fallen warrior laid on a bier, arms raised in grief as on ancient Greek funeral vases, torches against a dark sky.
ody.sapper: A Trojan saboteur creeping through the night with a torch and a pick, undermining the wooden palisade of the Greek camp.
ody.salve: Asclepius, the god of healing, with his staff entwined by a single serpent, gently applying a salve to a wounded warrior's arm.
ody.gale: The bag of winds of Aeolus torn open by Odysseus's crew: a howling gale bursts from the leather sack and hurls the ship back across the wine-dark sea, away from the shores of Ithaca.
ody.hammer: Hephaestus, the lame smith god, at his forge inside a volcano, hammer raised over the anvil, sparks and molten light flying.
ody.plunder: Raiders carrying golden vessels and a bronze tripod out of a burning temple at night, the cult statue watching from the flames.
ody.thunder: Zeus hurling a jagged thunderbolt from the storm clouds, striking Odysseus's ship at sea as punishment for eating the sacred cattle of Helios.
ody.bow: The great bow of Odysseus that none of the suitors could string, drawn at last in his hall, an arrow flying through the line of twelve axe-heads.
ody.owl: The little owl of Athena with wide golden eyes, gliding on silent wings over the moonlit Acropolis.
ody.iris: Iris, goddess of the rainbow and swift messenger of the gods, with golden wings, descending along a rainbow through storm clouds.
ody.helios: Helios the sun god, crowned with rays of light, driving his blazing four-horse chariot across the sky.
ody.nike: Nike, the winged goddess of victory, swooping down over a battlefield with a laurel wreath in her hand, her robes whipping in the wind.
ody.herm: Hermes, messenger of the gods, in his winged sandals and winged cap with his herald's staff, flying swiftly over the sea with a message from Olympus.
ody.eagle: The great golden eagle of Zeus with a thunderbolt clutched in its talons, wings spread wide against storm clouds.
ody.pegasus: Pegasus, the winged white horse born from the blood of Medusa, rearing in flight above the clouds at dawn.
ody.mino: The Minotaur, the bull-headed son of the Cretan queen, in the dark stone corridors of the Labyrinth at Knossos, torchlight and bones on the floor.
ody.cerb: Cerberus, the colossal three-headed hound of Hades, with a serpent for a tail and snakes along his back, snarling with glowing ember eyes at the gates of the underworld, the river Styx and green-black mist behind.
ody.tbull: The great white bull that Poseidon sent from the sea to King Minos, rising out of the waves onto the shore of Crete.
ody.charon: Charon, the grim old ferryman of the dead, poling his boat across the dark river Styx, pale shades waiting on the bank, a coin for the fare in his outstretched hand.
ody.capt: A veteran hoplite captain in a tall horsehair-crested helmet pointing his sword forward, ordering his shield line to advance.
ody.bastion: Spartan warriors in red cloaks standing shoulder to shoulder as a living wall before unwalled Sparta, because its men were its walls, Mount Taygetus behind.
ody.sack: Odysseus's men sacking and burning Ismarus, city of the Cicones, at night, the first raid on the voyage home from Troy.
ody.dio2: Diomedes the Bold driving his spear at the war god Ares himself with Athena's help, fire blazing from his helmet as the Iliad describes.
ody.muse: A Muse playing a lyre by a spring on Mount Helicon under the stars, a young poet listening, entranced.
ody.peltast: A light-armed Greek skirmisher with a crescent-shaped wicker shield, running and hurling a javelin.
ody.medic: Machaon, son of Asclepius and surgeon of the Greek army at Troy, binding a wounded warrior's leg inside a lamp-lit tent.
ody.pikeman: A guard of the Taphians, the sea-raiding people of the Odyssey, with a long pike and a hide shield, standing watch over a rocky harbour.
ody.veteran: A grey-bearded Athenian hoplite with old scars, standing on the marshy plain of Marathon, the burial mound of the fallen behind him.
ody.corsair: A Cicone raider from Thrace leaping from a small boat onto a beach, blade raised, painted shield on his arm.
ody.harrier: A raider blowing a horn from the prow of a ship as a pack of boats rushes into a harbour town at dawn.
ody.reaver: A hooded assassin in shadow dipping arrowheads into poison from a small clay pot, like the arrow-poison Odysseus sought at Ephyra.
ody.ram: Warriors under a wooden roof swinging a bronze-headed battering ram against a great city gate, splinters flying.
ody.augur: A seer like Calchas reading the flight of birds against a stormy sky, arms raised, the Greek fleet waiting below.
ody.sphinx: The Sphinx of Thebes, with a woman's face, a lion's body and an eagle's wings, perched on a rock outside the city to pose her riddle, bones scattered below.
ody.karma: The three Fates in a dark cave: one spinning the thread of life, one measuring it, one about to cut it with shears.
ody.leon: Leonidas, King of Sparta, a bearded king in a red cloak and a crested bronze helmet, holding a large round bronze shield, standing calm and proud in a narrow mountain pass at sunset.
ody.thermo: The narrow pass of Thermopylae between cliffs and the sea, a small line of Greek shields facing an endless Persian host at sunset.
ody.brasidas: Brasidas, the bold Spartan general, leading his men on a night march through the mountains of Thrace, red cloak and crested helmet in moonlight.
ody.pent: Penthesilea, queen of the Amazons, charging into battle at Troy on horseback with a double-headed axe and a crescent shield.
ody.horde: A mounted charge of Amazon warriors across a plain, axes and spears raised, horses at full gallop in a storm of dust.
ody.eury: Eurylochus, Odysseus's kinsman and second-in-command, a hard bearded sailor-warrior leading the crew ashore on Circe's island with a drawn sword, wary of the forest.
ody.iph: Iphigenia, daughter of Agamemnon, standing calmly at the altar at Aulis in a white robe as the goddess Artemis spirits her away and a deer appears in her place in a burst of light, the becalmed fleet behind.
ody.hades: Hades, Lord of the Dead, enthroned in the dark underworld with a dark crown and two-pronged staff, Cerberus at his feet, pale shades drifting in the distance.
ody.thanat: Thanatos, the winged god of death, a solemn dark-winged young man holding an upside-down extinguished torch, gliding silently over a battlefield at dusk.
ody.games: The funeral games for Patroclus at Troy: chariots racing around a turning post, the burial mound behind, crowds of warriors cheering.
ody.isl: A dazed islander of the Lotus-Eaters lying content in tall grass by the shore, a half-eaten lotus fruit in his hand, eyes heavy and dreaming.
ody.lot: A Lotus-Eater, a lean, smiling man crowned with lotus flowers, holding out the honey-sweet lotus fruit that makes travellers forget their way home.
ody.priest: A Poppy Priest of the Lotus-Eaters in a robe of red poppies, swinging a smoking censer, sweet drowsy smoke curling around him.
ody.reaper: A tall plant creature of woven lotus stems and drooping poppy heads, holding a crescent sickle, standing in a misty field of sleep.
ody.titan: A colossal stone giant asleep on the island of the Lotus-Eaters, overgrown with lotus vines, one heavy eye half open.
ody.sip: A hand offering a clay cup of honeyed lotus drink, sweet golden vapour rising from it, on a sunlit island shore.
ody.dream: Odysseus's sailors asleep in the long grass of the lotus island, smiling in their dreams, as dreamy mist drifts over them at dusk.
ody.censer: A bronze censer hanging from chains, pouring out thick, sweet-smelling poppy smoke in a dim island shrine.
ody.garden: The lush Lotus Garden of the Lotus-Eaters, pale lotus flowers and fruit trees under golden afternoon haze.
ody.fog: A creeping narcotic fog rolling over the beached black ships of Odysseus, sailors slumped drowsily on the oars.
ody.breeze: A warm, gentle island breeze sweeping through palms and lotus flowers on a sunlit shore, petals drifting in the air.
ody.lbow: A Lotus-Eater archer with a reed blowpipe and darts tipped with poppy, crouching among lotus flowers.
ody.nshade: A dark, glinting draught of nightshade in a small clay vessel, purple nightshade berries and leaves around it, faint violet vapour.
ody.lhz: A shimmering golden haze hanging over the island of the Lotus-Eaters, lotus flowers floating in the air, the sea faint and dreamlike.
ody.scout: A small Siren as the Greeks painted her, a woman's head on a bird's body, perched on a sea rock, watching for passing ships.
ody.song: A Siren with a woman's face and a bird's wings and body, singing from a rock in the sea, her song rippling visibly through the air.
ody.siren: A Siren of Anthemoessa, the flowery island of the Sirens: a bird-woman with great wings spread, singing among flowers above the sea, Odysseus's ship far below.
ody.eel: A huge moray eel lunging from a dark rocky crevice below the Sirens' island, jaws open, in green-blue water.
ody.lyre: A golden lyre resting on a sea-worn rock, its strings glowing faintly, waves breaking below at twilight.
ody.skies: A chorus of Sirens circling in a stormy twilight sky above the sea, wings wide, singing together.
ody.shoal: Jagged rocks just beneath the surface of a dark sea, foam breaking over them, a ship's broken oar caught among them.
ody.melody: Odysseus bound to the mast of his ship, straining against the ropes as the Sirens' enchanting melody washes over him, his crew rowing with wax in their ears.
ody.lure: The Sirens' meadow seen from the sea: flowers and a golden glow luring a ship toward hidden rocks.
ody.dirge: A sorrowful dirge of the deep: Sirens singing on a cliff under a pale moon, a lone bronze bell on a rock, a ghost-grey sea.
ody.canto: The Song of the Sirens made visible as golden ribbons of light flowing over the sea toward Odysseus's ship.
ody.sheep: A fat, woolly ram from the flock of Polyphemus standing in the Cyclops's cave, the kind Odysseus clung beneath to escape.
ody.cscout: A one-eyed Cyclops herder with a heavy stone hammer, standing on a hillside above his flocks on the island of the Cyclopes.
ody.cave: A shaggy cave beast with glowing eyes lurking in the dark mouth of a cave on the island of the Cyclopes, old bones on the ground.
ody.brute: A hulking one-eyed Cyclops warrior with a great wooden club, glaring, standing on rocky ground.
ody.elder: An ancient grey-bearded Cyclops elder with his single wise, weary eye, leaning on a gnarled staff outside his cave.
ody.poly: Polyphemus the Cyclops, son of Poseidon, the giant one-eyed shepherd standing at the mouth of his cave with a whole tree for a staff.
ody.hurl: Blinded Polyphemus hurling a huge boulder from the cliffs toward Odysseus's escaping ship, a great splash in the sea.
ody.club: The great olive-wood club of the Cyclops lying in his cave, as long as a ship's mast, beside a dying fire.
ody.mouth: The mouth of the Cyclops's cave sealed by an enormous boulder, firelight glowing through the gap, sheep pressed inside.
ody.shade1: A restless shade of the dead, a pale translucent figure drifting in grey mist at the edge of the underworld.
ody.mourner: A mourning shade, a veiled ghostly woman holding a withered rose, weeping in the gloom of Erebus.
ody.warden: A warden of the dead in dark bronze armour, standing guard before the gates of Erebus with a long spear.
ody.libation: Odysseus pouring a dark offering into a trench in the ground at the edge of the world, as pale shades gather to drink.
ody.pit: A dark pit at the edge of the underworld, pale ghostly hands and faces rising from its depths in the mist.
ody.hdead: The hungry dead of Hades crowding around a trench of dark offerings, pale and longing, in the grey twilight of Erebus.
ody.oarsman: A Phaeacian oarsman pulling at the oar of a swift, sleek ship on a calm sea, the island of Scheria behind.
ody.navig: A Phaeacian navigator at the stern of a ship that steers itself by thought alone, gazing at the stars above a calm sea.
ody.phguard: A guard of Scheria in polished bronze, standing before the gleaming golden gates of King Alcinous's palace.
ody.nausi: Nausicaa, the Phaeacian princess, by the river mouth where she and her maids washed clothes, turning in surprise as a stranger appears.
ody.alcinous: King Alcinous of the Phaeacians on his throne in a palace of bronze walls and golden doors, raising a cup in welcome.
ody.sails: The white sails of a Phaeacian ship filled with a favouring wind, racing over a bright sea.
ody.gift: A table of gifts of hospitality: a golden cup, a fine cloak, a tripod and bread and wine, set out for a guest in a Greek hall.
ody.tide: A gentle, glowing tide washing over a wounded warrior lying on a sunlit beach, healing light in the water.
ody.trident: The trident of Poseidon rising from a stormy sea, crackling with power, waves rearing around it.
ody.blackship: The swift black ship of the Phaeacians gliding home over a moonlit sea, the moment before Poseidon turns it to stone.
ody.mraid: A Cicone raider of Thrace with a battle axe and a round painted shield, charging out of the dawn mist.
ody.mskirm: A Cicone skirmisher with twin short swords, leaping over a low stone wall in the hills of Ismarus.
ody.mpill: A Cicone pillager carrying a flaming torch past a burning storehouse at night.
ody.chief: The chieftain of Ismarus, a fierce Thracian lord in a fur cloak and bronze helmet, holding a war banner on a hill.
ody.drums: Thracian war drums of hide and wood beaten at dawn on a hillside, warriors gathering in the mist behind.
ody.burn: Granaries burning in the night at Ismarus, sparks rising over the fields.
ody.javel: A volley of javelins arcing through a dawn sky over a beach where black ships are drawn up.
ody.cbow: A Cicone slinger whirling a leather sling above his head on a rocky hillside.
ody.hitr: Cicone horsemen wheeling away into the hills at dawn after striking the Greek camp, dust trailing behind them.
ody.cwolf: A great grey mountain wolf, enchanted by Circe, fawning gently with its tail wagging outside her stone palace on Aeaea.
ody.clion: A mountain lion of Aeaea, tame and strangely gentle under Circe's spell, prowling in the forest around her palace.
ody.cmaid: One of Circe's handmaids, a nymph of the springs and groves, carrying a silver bowl of healing herbs.
ody.circe: Circe, daughter of Helios, the enchantress of Aeaea, singing at her great loom in her stone hall, a golden wand at her side.
ody.cwand: Circe's golden wand glowing with enchantment, a faint swirl of light and a startled pig at her feet.
ody.cdraft: Circe's cup of drugged wine mixed with cheese, barley and honey, a faint green glow rising from it.
ody.cup: Circe's golden cup on a stone table in her palace, enchanted drink shimmering inside, pigs in the shadows behind.
ody.cow: A sacred cow of Helios, broad-browed with gilded horns, grazing in a golden meadow on the island of Thrinacia.
ody.bull: A massive sacred bull of Helios with a sun disc glowing between its horns, standing guard over the herd on Thrinacia.
ody.lamp: Lampetia, the shining nymph, daughter of Helios, herding her father's golden cattle across a sunlit meadow on Thrinacia.
ody.neith: Phaethusa, the radiant nymph, daughter of Helios, with a shepherd's crook, glowing softly at dawn among the sacred herd.
ody.scorch: A blinding ray of sunlight scorching down from the sky onto a rocky shore, the air shimmering with heat.
ody.sacril: The angry sun god Helios glaring down from his blazing chariot onto the island of Thrinacia, the sacred herd below.
ody.hmil: A Trojan militiaman, an ordinary townsman with a simple shield and spear, standing on the walls of Troy.
ody.hspr: A Trojan spearman in a crested helmet before the Scaean Gates of Troy, spear ready.
ody.hgua: An elite Ilian guard in heavy bronze armour with a tall rectangular shield, holding the gate of Troy.
ody.hchar: A Trojan charioteer driving two horses at full gallop across the plain of Troy.
ody.hector: Hector, Tamer of Horses and prince of Troy, in gleaming armour with a tall horse-hair crest, standing before the walls of Troy.
ody.priam: King Priam of Troy, a white-bearded old king in royal robes, looking out from the walls of his city.
ody.walls: The great walls of Troy rising over the plain at sunset, the Scaean Gates shut tight.
ody.sh1: One of Scylla's six heads on a long snake-like neck snapping out from a sea cave, rows of teeth bared.
ody.sh2: A gnashing head of Scylla on a long neck, emerging from the mist of her cliff cave, teeth bared.
ody.sh3: A head of Scylla that bays like a hound, its long neck stretched out from the cave, mouth open in a howl.
ody.sh4: A green, venomous head of Scylla on a long sinuous neck, dripping venom, lunging from the dark cave.
ody.scyl: Scylla, the six-headed monster of the strait, her six heads on long necks rising from her cave high in a sea cliff above a passing ship.
ody.curse: A withering curse: a dark, sickly mist curling around a bronze shield and helmet, tarnishing them as it spreads.
ody.heads: Scylla's six heads seen from the deck of a ship, rising from the cliff cave into the mist, each on its long neck.
ody.cdro: A drowned sailor's pale ghost rising from the dark sea, seaweed in his hair, eyes empty and sad.
ody.cspa: A small creature of swirling sea foam and spray, shaped like a crouching otter-like beast, rising from a churning patch of dark green sea near a rocky strait.
ody.ceel: A great eel coiling through the churning waters near Charybdis, sleek and fast.
ody.clev: A huge leviathan breaching from the dark sea near the whirlpool, its back like a reef.
ody.chary: Charybdis, the devouring whirlpool beneath the fig tree on the cliff, sucking down the dark sea into a vast spiral.
ody.undertow: A powerful undertow dragging a ship's anchor and rope down into the dark, swirling water.
ody.honey: A honeyed offering of cakes and a golden bowl of honey left on a sea rock to calm the waters.
ody.whirl: The whirlpool Charybdis seen from above, a vast spiral of dark sea, a ship's timbers caught at its rim.
ody.raidr: A young Ithacan raider leaping over the side of a black ship into the surf of a foreign beach, a short sword in one hand and a small round shield on his arm, salt-stiff hair flying, grinning with excitement.
ody.sunch: The chariot of the sun: Helios's golden chariot racing across the sky, drawn by four fiery horses with manes of flame, sparks streaming from its wheels, the god only a blinding silhouette at the reins. The chariot and horses are the whole picture.
ody.myrsh: A Myrmidon shield-bearer, one of Achilles' disciplined warriors from Phthia: a hard-faced hoplite in dark bronze armour and a black-crested helmet bracing a huge round shield painted with the ant emblem of the Myrmidons, feet planted, eyes cold over the rim.
ody.closer: Close ranks: a line of Greek hoplites slamming their round shields together into an overlapping wall at the shout of their officer, spears levelled over the rims, dust rising around their feet.
ody.horse: The Trojan Horse: the colossal wooden horse standing before the great walls of Troy at dawn, built from the timbers of the Greek ships and taller than the gate, a small hatch in its belly barely visible, tiny Trojans gathered in wonder at its hooves.
ody.dint: Divine intervention: a vast shining hand reaching down through parting storm clouds to catch a falling, wounded warrior just before he strikes the ground, pure golden light pouring through the gap in the clouds.

odin.brynh: Brynhild the valkyrie from the Volsunga saga, who defied Odin and was cast into an enchanted sleep inside a ring of fire on the mountain Hindarfjall: she stands awake at the heart of the wall of flame in a long iron mail byrnie and a plain iron helmet, gripping a spear and a round painted shield, her pale braids lifting in the heat, the fire ring closing around her on a dark snowy peak.
odin.star: Starkad, the ageless hero of the sagas, cursed by Thor and granted three lifetimes by Odin: a huge, grim old warrior with a long grey beard, a scarred, weathered face and hard eyes, a bearskin over battered mail, the haft of a great axe resting on his shoulder, snow settling on his hair; plain dark winter background.
odin.ygg: Yggdrasil, the world-ash: one immense, ancient ash tree, unmistakably a tree, standing alone on a rise above a sea of mist, its whole shape visible from the great spreading roots to the vast crown of branches; its roots sink into a glowing well at its foot. Only small details: an eagle silhouetted at the very top, and three tiny cloaked Norns at the roots for scale. Clean and simple, the tree is the whole picture.
odin.thor: Thor in full fury: the thunder god in mid-swing, hurling Mjolnir with one arm, lightning exploding from the hammer and wrapping around his whole body, his eyes blazing white with lightning, red hair and beard whipped upward by the storm, iron gauntlets and the belt of strength Megingjord, standing on a storm-lashed mountain peak. He looks utterly unstoppable.
odin.ulf: A young Ulfhednar initiate pulling a grey wolf pelt over his head and shoulders for the first time, the wolf skull resting on his brow, in a forest clearing at night lit by one fire, older wolf-coated warriors watching from the shadows, his eyes wide and wild.
odin.hugi: Huginn, Odin's raven of Thought: a black raven in flight whose spread wings and trailing feathers dissolve into glowing threads, flowing runes and branching lines of light like the paths of a thinking mind, a faint, vast outline of Odin's one-eyed face in the swirling light behind it.
odin.shmd: A Norse shield-maiden in the front rank of a shield wall on a pebble beach as longships land behind her: a young woman with a fierce, set face, braided hair under a plain iron helmet, her painted round wooden shield overlapping her neighbours' and a spear levelled, sea-spray and sleet in the air.
odin.loki: Loki in hiding after Baldr's death, from the Prose Edda: the sly, red-haired trickster sits in his remote mountain house by the fire, knotting the very first fishing net from linen cord, glancing sideways as if he hears the gods coming, a waterfall visible through the open door.
odin.odn: Odin the Allfather in all his power: a tall, gaunt old king with one blazing eye and a dark empty socket, long grey beard, a wide-brimmed hat and a dark blue cloak over mail, gripping the spear Gungnir; his two ravens Huginn and Muninn close at his shoulders. A cold wind and a dark sky behind him; nothing else competes with him.
odin.bald: Baldr the Beautiful, the shining god whom nothing could harm: a young, serene god with pale gold hair, a calm face and a faint cold light about him, in a white wool tunic with a gold-trimmed cloak, a sprig of mistletoe drifting in the air near him as an omen of his death. Simple dark winter background.
odin.sigur: Sigurd the Dragon-Slayer from the Volsunga saga, just after slaying the dragon Fafnir: the young hero kneels by a fire, the reforged sword Gram across his knees, licking dragon's blood from his burnt thumb and suddenly understanding the speech of the birds; a single bird on a branch above him. Fafnir is only a dark coil of scales at the very edge of the picture.
odin.slei: Sleipnir, Odin's eight-legged grey horse, the finest of all steeds: a powerful, storm-grey stallion with eight legs, wild mane and steaming breath, galloping through the air above the clouds, runes carved on its bridle; empty, bare saddle.
odin.mjol: Mjolnir, the hammer of Thor: the short-handled iron hammer alone, resting on a snow-covered runestone, its head carved with interlaced beasts, lightning crackling faintly around it and melting the snow beneath. The hammer is the whole picture.
odin.norn: The Norns, Urd, Verdandi and Skuld, who weave the fate of gods and men: three tall cloaked women, one old, one in her prime, one young and veiled, standing together at the well beneath the roots of the world-tree and carving runes of fate into a wooden staff as glowing threads run between their hands.
odin.valk: A valkyrie, a chooser of the slain, riding a dark horse low over a misty battlefield at dusk: a stern young woman in mail and a plain iron helmet with a spear, her cloak streaming, reaching down toward a fallen warrior to carry him to Valhalla.
odin.bsrk: A Bear-Shirt berserker in the grip of battle-fury: a huge bearded warrior wearing a bear's head and pelt as a cloak, biting the rim of his round wooden shield, eyes rolled wild, an axe raised; snow and sparks around him.
odin.rser: A rune-carver at work: an old bearded man in a fur hood kneeling before a tall grey runestone, carving a serpent band of runes with chisel and mallet, painting the cut lines red by the light of a small fire.
odin.idun: Idunn's apples, the apples of youth that keep the gods young: three ripe golden apples, clearly apples with stems and leaves, resting in a simple carved ash-wood bowl lined with moss, a soft golden light coming from the fruit; frost on the wood around them.
odin.howl: A war howl before battle: a wolf-coated warrior with his head thrown back and mouth wide open, howling up at a huge full moon, the wolf skull of his pelt over his brow, breath steaming in the cold, the shapes of his warband dim in the mist behind him.
odin.volv: The volva, a Norse seeress: a woman in a dark blue cloak and a black lambskin hood lined with white cat fur, seated on a high platform, holding her iron staff topped with a brass knob, eyes half-closed in a trance as smoke curls around her in a dim hall.
odin.hird: A hirdman, a sworn warrior of a Norse lord's household: a sturdy bearded man in a mail shirt and a plain iron helmet with a nose guard, a round painted wooden shield on his arm and a spear held ready, standing guard at the door of a longhall.
odin.thrl: A thrall, a Norse bondsman: a thin, ragged young man with a shaved head and an iron collar, in a coarse undyed wool tunic, gripping a wood-axe as he is pushed into battle, fear and stubborn hope in his face.
odin.gung: Gungnir's throw: the spear Gungnir, its head carved with runes, flying straight at the viewer through the air, trailing cold light, the hand that threw it only a shadow far behind. The spear is the whole picture.
odin.oath: A blood oath: two warriors' hands clasped over a ring of iron, a thin line of blood running from a fresh cut across each palm into a bowl, a knife and a runestone beside it, firelight on the scene.
odin.fjrd: A fjord raider leaping from the prow of a longship onto a rocky shore: a young Norse raider in leather and fur with an axe and a round shield, the carved dragon prow rising behind him, spray flying.
odin.skar: Skar the Scarred, a veteran berserker: a grizzled warrior with a face crossed by old scars and one milky eye, braided beard, bare scarred arms and a notched sword, grinning grimly.
odin.wulf: A wolf-coat warrior charging: an ulfhednar with a grey wolf pelt over his head and back, bared teeth, a spear in each hand, running low through a snowy birch forest.
odin.gslay: A giant-slayer standing triumphant on the chest of a fallen frost giant whose huge body stretches across the picture like a snowy hill, his axe raised high over his head, ice crystals in the giant's enormous beard, a tiny figure against a vast pale sky.
odin.egil: Egil the Mad, the poet-warrior of Egil's saga: a huge, ugly, heavy-browed man with a wild beard, laughing as he chants a verse with an axe in his fist, drinking horn in the other hand, firelit.
odin.blod: A blood-drinker berserker: a gaunt warrior with blood smeared across his mouth and chest, drinking from a horn of blood before battle, wild eyes, a bearskin over his shoulders.
odin.skul: The Skull-Cleaver, a Norse champion: a broad warrior in mail with a huge bearded axe raised in both hands, mid-swing, wood splinters and snow flying.
odin.ulfk: Ulf, the Berserk King: a towering king of the wolf-warriors, wearing a great black wolf pelt like a mantle and an iron circlet, his bare chest painted with runes, a huge two-handed axe resting on his shoulder.
odin.bldr: A blood rite: a bowl of blood held up over a stone altar by a priest's hands, the blood splashed across a carved runestone and running into the snow.
odin.rage: Berserkergang, the battle-fury: a berserker's face in extreme close-up, teeth bared, veins standing out, eyes rolled and wild, foam at his mouth and a shield rim between his teeth.
odin.mhall: Mead-hall fury: a wide view down the length of a long, firelit mead hall in the middle of a wild brawl: benches overturned, drinking horns and mead flying through the air, a dozen warriors wrestling, roaring and swinging fists around the long central hearth.
odin.rend: The skull-splitter: a great bearded axe buried in a split iron helmet on a battlefield, snow and blood around it. The axe and helmet are the whole picture.
odin.roar: Roar of the wolf-coats: a pack of wolf-pelted warriors roaring together in a line, faces up, weapons raised, the shock of their roar bending the snow and mist around them.
odin.sprm: A spear-marked thrall: a young bondsman with a red mark of a spear painted on his chest, kneeling with his head bowed as an offering to Odin before battle, rope around his wrists.
odin.gash: A spear-gash: a warrior pressing his hand to a fresh wound on his side, blood between his fingers, gritting his teeth with fierce resolve, spear still in his other hand.
odin.hamr: Hamramr the shape-shifter, mid-transformation: a warrior whose head has become a snarling brown bear's head with a muzzle and fangs while his body is still a man in torn mail and a cloak, one hand still human and the other a huge clawed bear's paw, howling under the aurora in a dark forest.
odin.lstd: The last stand of the doomed: three battered warriors back to back on a hilltop, shields up and weapons out, surrounded and outnumbered, fierce and unafraid.
odin.thegn: A thegn of the hall, kneeling: a young retainer in a fine red embroidered tunic kneeling on one knee before his lord's high seat and offering his sword up hilt-first with both hands, his head bowed, firelight from the long hearth on his face; only the lord's legs and the carved high seat are visible.
odin.einw: An einherjar warrior, one of the slain heroes of Valhalla: a warrior with healed battle wounds and a calm, proud face, in mail and a gold-trimmed cloak, holding a sword, light from the shields that roof Valhalla falling on him.
odin.skld: A skald of the fallen: a grey-haired poet sitting by a fire with a lyre, singing of the dead, the faces of slain warriors faint in the smoke above him.
odin.eir: Eir the healer, goddess of healing: a calm woman in a pale green cloak kneeling beside a wounded warrior, holding a bowl of herbs and a cup, her hands glowing faintly.
odin.huscl: A housecarl, a lord's bodyguard: a huge warrior with a long Dane-axe and a kite shield, standing in front of his lord with his feet planted, unmovable.
odin.jarl: The fallen jarl: a dead Norse lord lying in state in a ship-grave, in his best armour with his sword on his chest and his shield at his feet, grave goods around him, a crowd of mourners as dim shapes.
odin.ghall: The hall of the slain: the great hall of Valhalla, its roof made of golden shields and its rafters of spears, long tables of feasting warriors, seen down its full length.
odin.vfea: The feast of heroes: a great roasting boar on a spit over a long fire in Valhalla, horns of mead raised by warriors' hands around it.
odin.host: The host of Valhalla: a line of ghostly einherjar warriors riding out of a cloud bank on horseback, shields and spears catching the light, led by a valkyrie.
odin.ofr: A pyre of heroes, seen from a distance: a tall, square funeral pyre of stacked logs blazing on a bare headland above a dark sea at night, a warrior's cloaked body lying on top of it, flames and sparks streaming up into the sky, a few small mourners in silhouette below. The pyre is clearly a stacked pile of logs.
odin.vmar: Marshalling the dead: a warlord raising his sword in a cold fog, the faint spirits of his fallen warriors rising behind him to stand in ranks.
odin.hguard: A hall-guard of Valhalla: a giant warrior in gold-trimmed mail standing at one of Valhalla's five hundred and forty doors, a spear crossed in front of the door.
odin.scav: A battlefield scavenger: a hunched figure in a hooded cloak picking through the shields and swords of the fallen on a misty battlefield at dawn, a raven on a broken spear beside him.
odin.stdb: A standard-bearer: a young warrior holding high a tall pole with a raven banner streaming in the wind, shouting the warband forward.
odin.slst: A slain-strike: a ghostly spear thrown by a dead warrior's spirit, glowing pale as it flies over a battlefield.
odin.gunn: Gunnar, the hall-warden: a strong, gallant warrior at the gates of a hall, sword drawn and shield up, his long hair tied back, ready to hold the doorway alone.
odin.muni: Muninn, Odin's raven of Memory: a black raven perched on an old moss-covered runestone, and drifting out of its dark feathers like smoke are faint, ghostly scenes of the past: a longship at sea, a burning hall, warriors long dead, all fading into mist; its one bright eye holds a tiny reflected memory.
odin.skal: A skaldic bard: a young poet standing on a bench in a crowded hall, reciting with one arm raised, a gold arm-ring flashing.
odin.fylg: A fylgja, a guardian spirit: a translucent white she-wolf of light walking beside a sleeping warrior in the snow, watching over him.
odin.hrav: Hrafnagud, the raven-god: Odin as a great shadowy raven-shape with outstretched wings and one glowing eye, its feathers turning into a dark cloak.
odin.ruru: Uruz, the rune of strength: the rune Uruz carved deep into a standing stone, glowing, with the great horns of a wild aurochs rising behind it in the mist.
odin.alg: Algiz, the rune of protection: the rune Algiz shining on the face of a round wooden shield, a protective light flaring outward from it.
odin.fehu: Fehu, the rune of wealth: the rune Fehu carved into a gold arm-ring on top of a heap of silver hacksilver and coins in a wooden chest.
odin.reir: The rune of Eir: a small wooden rune-stave carved with a healing rune, tied with red thread and hanging from a warrior's belt, glowing softly.
odin.mimr: Mimir's well: the severed, living head of the wise god Mimir resting at the edge of a dark pool beneath the roots of the world-tree, his eyes open and knowing, Odin's eye shining at the bottom of the water.
odin.rfly: The raven banner: a white triangular war banner with a black raven on it, streaming in a strong wind on a tall pole, its raven seeming to flap its wings.
odin.gald: Galdr of winds: a rune-singer on a cliff edge chanting with her arms out, the wind she calls tearing at her cloak and hair and whipping the sea below.
odin.seid: A seidr hex: a sorceress's hands weaving a curse in the air, threads of dark light spinning from her fingers around a carved staff.
odin.tiwa: Tiwaz, the rune of victory: the arrow-shaped rune Tiwaz cut into a spearhead, glowing hot, the spear held up against the sky.
odin.scrb: A rune-scribe: a young woman carefully cutting runes into a wooden stick with a small knife by candlelight, a row of finished rune-staves before her.
odin.ansu: Ansuz, the rune of speech: the rune Ansuz glowing in the air in front of an old storyteller's open mouth as he speaks.
odin.hagl: Hagalaz, the rune of hail: a storm of huge hailstones falling from a black sky onto a battlefield, the rune Hagalaz flashing in the clouds.
odin.tyr: Tyr the one-handed, god of war and oaths: a stern, broad-shouldered god with one hand missing at the wrist, holding his sword in the other, the shadow of the wolf Fenrir who bit off his hand looming faintly behind him.
odin.hela: Hel's embrace: the goddess Hel, half of her face pale and beautiful and half dark and dead, reaching out her arms in a cold, gloomy underworld.
odin.vlnd: Volund the smith: the legendary master smith at his forge, hammering a glowing sword on the anvil, sparks flying, his face grim and determined.
odin.mead: The mead of poetry: a great carved drinking horn overflowing with golden mead that glows with light, held up in a dark hall.
odin.pup: A wolf pup of Fenrir's brood: a small, fierce black wolf cub with oversized paws and glowing yellow eyes, snarling on a snowy rock, already showing its fangs.
odin.wolf: A great grey wolf of the iron wood, running flat out through deep snow, its whole lean body stretched in mid-leap, snow spraying from its paws, pine trunks streaking past.
odin.hati: Hati, the wolf who chases the moon: an enormous pale silver wolf leaping across the night sky toward a huge full moon, its jaws open, stars caught in its fur.
odin.skoll: Skoll, the wolf who chases the sun: an enormous red-gold wolf racing across a dawn sky after a low, pale sun, its fur streaming like fire.
odin.fenr: Fenrir unbound: the monstrous wolf, as big as a hall, his jaws opened so wide they touch earth and sky, the broken silken fetter Gleipnir hanging from his neck, eyes burning, the world shaking around him.
odin.pgrow: The pack grows: a ring of glowing wolf eyes in the darkness of a snowy forest at night, more and more pairs appearing between the trees, one great black wolf at the centre.
odin.ithrl: A frost thrall: a gaunt spirit made of ice and frozen mist in the shape of a man, its body cracked and glittering, frost spreading from its feet across the stones.
odin.rimew: A rime-witch, a giantess of the frost: a tall, gaunt jotun woman with blue-white skin and hair like icicles, raising a hand that freezes the air into a spiral of ice.
odin.hgnt: A hill giant: a huge, craggy giant with skin like grey stone and moss in his beard, rising from a mountainside with a tree trunk for a club, tiny pines at his knees.
odin.icesp: An ice spear: a long jagged spear of blue ice flying through a snowstorm, frost trailing behind it. The spear is the whole picture.
odin.rwall: The rimewall: a towering wall of blue glacier ice blocking a mountain pass, with huge frost giants dimly visible inside the ice like shadows.
odin.dmin: A dwarf miner: a short, broad dwarf with a braided beard and a leather cap, swinging a pick at a glowing seam of gold in a dark tunnel, lantern on his belt.
odin.dsmith: A dwarf smith: a stocky dwarf with a singed beard and leather apron, lifting a red-hot blade from the forge with tongs, sparks around him.
odin.dxbow: A dwarf crossbowman: a helmeted dwarf in heavy mail kneeling behind a rock and aiming a heavy iron crossbow straight at the viewer.
odin.brokk: Brokkr, the master smith who forged Mjolnir: an old dwarf with a huge white beard pumping a great bellows with all his might while a fly stings his eyelid, the forge blazing.
odin.golem: An iron golem forged by the dwarves: a hulking figure of riveted black iron plates and glowing rune seams, steam venting from its joints, its fists like anvils.
odin.anvl: The anvil of Eitri: a great black iron anvil carved with runes, glowing red-hot with a half-forged ring of gold on it, a hammer resting beside it. The anvil is the whole picture.
odin.dshld: A dwarf-forged shield: a round shield of dark iron and gold inlay with an interlaced dragon pattern, hanging on the stone wall of a forge, firelight on its boss.
odin.drpn: Draupnir, the ring of gold: a thick gold arm-ring with eight smaller rings dripping from it like drops, resting on black velvet-dark stone, glowing softly.
odin.dbolt: A dwarven bolt: a heavy iron crossbow bolt with rune-cut fins, glowing hot, flying out of the dark toward the viewer.
odin.ffire: The forge-fire: the great forge of the dwarves blazing inside a mountain hall, molten gold pouring from a crucible into a mould, the whole cavern lit gold and red.
odin.ember: An ember sprite: a small, flickering fire spirit shaped like a laughing imp made of embers and sparks, darting over glowing coals.
odin.fraid: A flame raider of Muspelheim: a warrior with skin like cracked charcoal glowing with lava beneath, a burning sword in his hand, flames for hair.
odin.lava: A lava hound: a hound made of black volcanic rock with molten lava glowing through the cracks, flames dripping from its jaws, prowling over a lava field.
odin.mgnt: A Muspel giant: a towering fire giant with skin of glowing rock and a beard of flame, raising a burning axe against a sky of smoke and fire.
odin.surtr: Surtr, lord of Muspelheim: the black fire giant with a flaming sword brighter than the sun, his face dark and terrible, a crown of flames, standing amid a sea of fire.
odin.fbolt: A searing bolt: a lance of white-hot fire streaking from a dark sky toward the ground, scorching the snow into steam.
odin.mspear: A molten spear: a spear of glowing molten rock dripping fire as it flies through smoke.
odin.bland: Scorched earth: a burnt Norse farmstead, charred longhouse frames and blackened fields smoking under a red sky, embers drifting.
odin.draug: A draugr, a restless corpse risen from its grave mound: a bloated, blue-black dead warrior in rotted mail with pale glowing eyes, climbing out of a barrow at night.
odin.wight: A barrow-wight: a gaunt, skeletal dead king in a crown and rotted robes, sitting on a throne inside his burial mound among his grave goods, cold light in his eyes.
odin.hgrd: A Hel-guard: a tall armoured guardian of Hel's gate, half its body fleshless bone, holding a long spear before the black gate of the underworld.
odin.nidh: Nidhogg, the corpse-gnawer: the black dragon of the dead coiled among the dark roots beneath the world, gnawing a root with its huge fanged jaws, its scales dull as ash.
odin.hgrasp: The grasp of the grave: pale dead hands bursting up through cold earth and snow to seize a warrior's ankles.
odin.corp: Corpse-cold: the grey, frozen realm of Hel, a field of frost-covered dead warriors standing silent in the mist, all facing the same way.
odin.lrav: Loki's raven: a sly black raven with an unnaturally knowing grin, perched on a twisted branch, a stolen gold ring glinting in its beak, purple dusk behind it.
odin.imp: A sly imp: a small, grinning trickster spirit with pointed ears and long fingers, perched on a drinking horn and pouring mead into a sleeping warrior's ear.
odin.skinw: A skin-changer: a figure halfway through turning from a man into a fox, their body twisting, half of the face a sly fox's muzzle.
odin.lokis: Loki the shapeshifter: the red-haired trickster god grinning as he changes shape, his body breaking into a flock of birds, a salmon and a mare at the edges of his cloak.
odin.lsnare: Loki's trick: a warrior frozen mid-step, tangled in near-invisible glowing threads, a sly shadow of Loki laughing behind him.
odin.lcurse: Loki's mischief: a warrior staring in horror as his sword turns into a snake in his hand.
odin.lgale: A wind of mischief: a sudden whirlwind of leaves and snow sweeping a warrior off his feet, a laughing face in the swirl of wind.
odin.lokib: Barbed words: Loki at a feast, leaning forward with a cruel smile and pointing, his insults shown as sharp glowing thorns flying from his mouth.
odin.ltax: Loki's toll: a grinning Loki holding out his open palm for payment at a narrow bridge, a pile of gold rings at his feet.
odin.urd: Urd, keeper of the past: an ancient woman in grey robes with white hair, holding a spindle of old faded threads, sitting at the edge of a glowing well.
odin.verd: Verdandi, weaver of the present: a woman in her prime at a great loom, weaving a shining tapestry of fate, her hands quick and sure.
odin.skuld: Skuld, maiden of the future: a young woman with her face hidden by a veil, holding a pair of shears and a scroll of runes, half valkyrie, a spear at her side.
odin.nspin: A thread-spinner: a hooded figure spinning a single glowing thread from a distaff, the thread running out of the picture.
odin.nwarr: A doomed warrior: a young warrior standing calm and resigned, a single golden thread of fate running from his chest and about to be cut by shears above him.
odin.ndoom: A doom decree: a runestone carved with a sentence of fate glowing red, a crack splitting through it.
odin.fate: The well of Urd: a deep, still well beneath the vast roots of the world-tree, its water glowing silver-white, swans gliding on its surface.
odin.fafn: Fafnir the hoard-dragon: a huge serpentine dragon coiled on a mountain of gold rings and treasure, its scales glinting gold, its eyes greedy and burning.
odin.fgrd: A hoard-guard: a grim armoured warrior standing guard in a treasure cave, gold to his knees, his eyes gone gold with greed.
odin.fworm: A lindworm: a long, limbless wingless dragon-serpent with two clawed forelegs, slithering through a dark marsh, its jaws open.
odin.regin: Regin the smith: a cunning, scheming dwarf smith with a crooked smile, reforging the broken sword Gram at his anvil.
odin.dbrth: Dragon's breath: a torrent of fire and poison pouring from an unseen dragon's jaws across a rocky slope, scorching everything in its path.
odin.fspit: Venom spit: a glob of green venom flying from a dragon's mouth, hissing as it spatters on a shield and melts the wood.
odin.hoard: The hoard of Andvari: a heap of gold rings, cups and coins glittering in a cave, with the cursed ring Andvaranaut at the top shining brightest.
odin.jsnk: A sea-snake, child of the World Serpent: a huge green-scaled sea serpent rising out of grey waves, its head reared high, water streaming off it.
odin.jcrw: A brine-wyrm attacking a longship: a barnacle-crusted sea beast coiling around a small Viking longship, its long body looping over and under the hull, the crew tiny on the deck.
odin.jorm: Jormungandr, the World Serpent: the vast serpent that circles the world rising from the ocean, its head enormous against a stormy sky, venom dripping from its fangs, the sea boiling around it.
odin.jbck: The deep takes back: a huge dark wave rising over a beach and pulling warriors and boats out to sea.
odin.jgrp: A drowning grip: the coils of a sea serpent wrapping around a longship and dragging it under the waves.
odin.jspt: Venom spray: a spray of glowing green venom bursting from beneath the sea's surface across a ship's deck.
odin.ouro: The ouroboros: the World Serpent biting its own tail, its body forming a vast ring around a small dark world in a black sea.
odin.hhnd: A Hel-hound of the Wild Hunt: a black ghost-hound with burning eyes and smoke streaming from its fur, running through a stormy night sky.
odin.hrdr: A phantom rider: a pale, translucent rider on a skeletal horse, galloping through the clouds with a spear, his cloak torn by the wind.
odin.hwld: A wild huntsman: a cloaked rider with a hunting horn at his lips, mounted on a black horse, leaping across the storm clouds.
odin.hmst: The huntmaster of the Gandreid: a grim, one-eyed leader of the Wild Hunt in a wide hat, riding a great horse at the head of a ghostly host through the night sky.
odin.hhrn: The horn of the hunt: a great carved hunting horn blown in the storm, its sound shown as rings of ghostly light spreading across the sky.
odin.hhbt: A hunter's spear: a long ghostly spear flying through a stormy night sky, trailing pale light.
odin.hunt: The Wild Hunt: a host of ghostly riders and hounds sweeping across a stormy winter night sky above a small frightened village.
odin.hrung: Hrungnir, the stone-hearted, strongest of the giants: a colossal giant with a head and heart of stone, carrying a great stone shield and a whetstone club, standing on a barren mountain.
odin.hmokk: Mokkurkalfi, the clay giant built by the giants to fight Thor: a huge, lumpy, red-brown giant of wet clay standing knee-deep in a muddy plain, rain streaming down him, cracks in his body and a frightened mare's heart glowing through a gap in his chest; tiny warriors at his feet for scale.
odin.htrl: A rock-troll: a hunched troll with skin like lichen-covered stone, long arms and a tusked jaw, lurking at the mouth of a cave.
odin.hgrt: A gravel giant: a huge giant whose whole body is built of stacked boulders and loose gravel, clearly a giant with a head, arms and legs, striding down a mountain slope with stones and dust pouring off him at every step, his eyes two glowing cracks; a few pines at his ankles for scale.
odin.hwhet: The whetstone of Hrungnir: a huge jagged whetstone hurled through the air, shattering as it meets a lightning bolt.
odin.hmead: Giant's mead: an enormous drinking horn overflowing with mead, held in a giant's stone hand.
odin.holm: The holmgang: two warriors facing each other in a duel inside a square marked by hazel stakes and a cloak spread on the ground, shields up.
odin.bodvar: Bodvar Bjarki, the bear-spirit hero of Hrolf Kraki's saga: a huge, calm warrior sitting as if asleep while the great spirit of a red-brown bear rises from his body behind him, the bear towering and roaring, its form half solid and half mist.
odin.vinit: A Valhalla initiate: a young warrior, freshly slain, standing uncertainly at the golden doors of Valhalla in his torn and bloodied tunic, a valkyrie's hand on his shoulder guiding him in.
odin.freyja: Freyja, lady of the slain, who takes half of those who die in battle to her hall Folkvangr: a beautiful, fierce goddess with golden hair, wearing the shining necklace Brisingamen and a cloak of falcon feathers, standing on a battlefield with her hand raised over the fallen.
odin.othala: Othala, the rune of heritage: the rune Othala carved deep into the door-post of an old ancestral longhouse, glowing softly, with the carved faces of ancestors around it.
odin.bragi: Bragi, god of poetry: a long-bearded god with runes tattooed on his tongue, singing with a golden harp, the words of his song turning into glowing runes that drift around him in the air.

wukong.wking: Sun Wukong, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, in his full glory: the Monkey King with golden fur and blazing fiery golden eyes, wearing a phoenix-feather cap with two long pheasant plumes, golden chain mail, a red silk cape and cloud-walking boots, spinning his golden-banded iron staff Ruyi Jingu Bang above his head, standing on a swirl of auspicious cloud. Proud, fearless and grinning.
wukong.wpig: Zhu Bajie, the Pig of the Eight Prohibitions, once Marshal of the Heavenly Canopy: a huge pot-bellied pig-faced warrior with big floppy ears and a greedy, cheerful grin, in a loose black monk's robe, swinging his nine-toothed iron muckrake over his shoulder.
wukong.wmount: The Five Elements Mountain: the Buddha's giant open palm turning into five stone peaks that press down on the tiny Monkey King trapped beneath, a golden paper talisman with the six-syllable mantra sealing the summit; only Wukong's furious head and one arm stick out from the rock.
wukong.wfan: The mountain-felling gale: Princess Iron Fan, in red and gold silk robes, swinging her giant palm-leaf fan with both hands, and the typhoon it unleashes roaring away from her as a spiralling wall of wind that tears trees and rocks from a mountainside.
wukong.wclone: Clones of the Great Sage: Sun Wukong blowing on a handful of plucked golden hairs that turn mid-air into a crowd of identical little monkey warriors with staffs, each tumbling and grinning.
wukong.wpeachk: A peach keeper of the Heavenly Peach Garden: a small, mischievous monkey sitting on a gnarled branch of the immortal peach tree, cradling a huge glowing peach and taking a big bite, peach blossoms falling around it.
wukong.wfurn: The Eight-Trigram Furnace of Laozi: the great bronze cauldron-furnace engraved with the eight trigrams, blazing with fire, the lid bursting open as the Monkey King leaps out unharmed, his eyes now burning gold from the smoke.
wukong.wcloudm: A cloud rider: a young monkey warrior crouched on a small curling cloud as if surfing, racing through the sky past misty mountain peaks, its tail streaming behind.
